skill.name: ab-test-setup
skill.description: Plan statistically sound A/B tests with hypotheses, variants, sample sizes, metrics, traffic allocation, and result documentation.
skill.summary: Design A/B experiments with clear hypotheses, metrics, sample sizes, and analysis plans.

content.value_statement: Teams risk inconclusive experiments when hypotheses, metrics, and sample sizes are unclear. This skill structures A/B tests so decisions use reliable evidence.
actual_capabilities: Builds hypotheses using observation, expected effect, audience, and success metrics.
Selects A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, or split URL test formats.
Estimates sample size and duration from baseline rate, MDE, traffic, power, and significance.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for common test types.
Creates test plans with variants, traffic allocation, implementation approach, and analysis criteria.
Summarizes results with decisions, actions, learnings, and next tests.
limitations: Does not install analytics tracking or write production experiment code.
Requires reliable baseline conversion rates and traffic estimates from the user.
Sample size references are approximate and should be verified with a calculator or statistics tool.
Cannot guarantee statistical validity if tests stop early or tracking data is incomplete.

use_cases.title: Plan a Landing Page Test
use_cases.description: Create a clear test plan for headline, CTA, layout, or social proof changes.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Product Experiments
use_cases.description: Turn product ideas into measurable experiments with variants, metrics, and decision rules.

use_cases.title: Review Experiment Results
use_cases.description: Assess significance, practical impact, guardrails, and next actions after a test ends.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an A/B test for [page or flow]. Current conversion is [rate], daily traffic is [number], and the proposed change is [change].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a simple experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Hypothesis and Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this test idea: [idea]. Turn it into a clear hypothesis and define primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a test idea needs sharper measurement.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Sample Size and Duration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the sample size approach for a test with [baseline rate], [MDE], [daily traffic], [variants], 95% confidence, and 80% power.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before launch to check whether traffic can support the test.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Experiment Program Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete experiment brief for [business goal]. Include hypothesis, variants, allocation, QA, analysis plan, risks, decision rules, and learning repository notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a stakeholder-ready experiment plan.

output_examples.input: Plan an A/B test for a pricing page headline with 8,000 daily visitors and a 4% plan selection rate.
output: Hypothesis links the headline change to clearer value perception and higher plan selection.
Recommended design is a 50/50 A/B test with one headline change and stable pricing content.
Metrics include plan selection as primary, time on page as secondary, and refund rate as guardrail.
Duration depends on the minimum detectable effect and should cover at least one business cycle.

output_examples.input: Review a completed signup flow test with a 6% lift but weaker activation after signup.
output: Result needs both statistical and practical significance before rollout.
Lower activation is a guardrail concern and may outweigh the signup lift.
Recommended action is segment review, quality analysis, and a follow-up test before full launch.

output_examples.input: Create documentation for a landing page CTA experiment.
output: Document includes test name, dates, owner, hypothesis, variants, metrics, decision, action, and learnings.
Variant notes describe the CTA copy and placement changes without altering unrelated page elements.
Learning repository notes capture why the test was run and what should be tested next.

best_practices: Predefine the hypothesis, sample size, duration, and decision criteria before launch.
Use one primary metric and guardrail metrics tied to revenue, retention, or user quality.
Keep variants stable during the test and document external factors.
anti_patterns: Stopping a test early because the current result looks significant.
Testing multiple unrelated changes without enough traffic for reliable attribution.
Calling a winner from segment data that was not planned before launch.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the right A/B test type?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares A/B, A/B/n, multivariate, and split URL tests based on traffic, scope, and complexity.

faq.question: Does it calculate exact sample sizes?
faq.answer: It provides planning estimates and inputs. Final sample sizes should be verified with a statistics tool or calculator.

faq.question: Can it implement tracking code?
faq.answer: No. It can define tracking requirements, but analytics setup should be handled by a tracking or engineering workflow.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the current conversion rate, traffic volume, proposed change, goal metric, and smallest useful improvement.

faq.question: Can it help after a test finishes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure result summaries, review guardrails, explain inconclusive outcomes, and recommend next tests.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code marketplace workflows.
